label: Corning ADSS 96F aerial, G.652.D
notes: Corning 096ELE-T3322A20 product spec sheet (Corning Optical Communications ecatalog, revision date 2026-11-28): Aerial Dielectric Self-Supporting Cable, ADSS 96 F Single-mode (OS2), A-D2Y(T)2Y, (8 x 12). Eight active loose tubes of 12 fibres in eight tube positions - the 96-fibre core fills every position, so this size carries no filling elements where the 12F, 24F and 48F rungs carry eleven, ten and eight - dielectric central element, DRY core held by swellable elements rather than gel, non-metallic (aramid) strength members over the core, black PE jacket, halogen-free, one ripcord; construction A-D2Y(T)2Y per EN 60794-1-1 (DIN VDE 0888-100-1); 19.9 mm nominal diameter, 198 kg/km, crush 3000 N/10 cm, max tensile 1700 N long-term / 4000 N short-term, min bend radius 350 mm installation / 300 mm operation, -40 to +70 C operating and storage (-5 to +50 C installation), Telcordia colour code, ITU-T G.652.D / IEC 60793-2-50 B1.3 fibre, cable cutoff 1260 nm, PMD link design value <= 0.06 ps/sqrt(km). Why the row exists: the aerial family stopped at 48F (g652d-adss-12 / -24 / -48), and the 48F row already recorded the sheet line single-layer stranded construction up to 144 fibres as proof that a larger aerial feeder is a part this vendor stocks rather than a different construction - but no row named it. A pole-route feeder above 48F therefore had only g652d-loose-96 or g652d-ribbon-96 to name, both gel-filled duct and underground cable with no self-supporting strength member, so the BOM bought a cable the route cannot take. Measured on this engine: a 1,200 m 96-fibre span answers g652d-loose-96 from a ladder that stocks only the duct rungs, and g652d-adss-96 once this row is in the ladder (equal 96-fibre counts, tie broken on model id, g652d-adss-96 first). This is the 96F rung; 144F is g652d-adss-144, and the two close the up-to-144 the 48F row cited. Attenuation, and exactly what kind of figure it is: the sheet publishes MAXIMUM 0.36 dB/km at 1310 nm, 0.36 at 1383 nm and 0.22 at 1550 nm - maxima, not typicals, and no 1490 nm figure at all. This row carries 0.35 / 0.22 / 0.21, the same typical installed row every other cable here carries, deliberately: budgeting one aerial span at a factory maximum while its duct neighbours are budgeted at typicals prices the same design two different ways. 1490 nm is interpolated between the two published windows and is not a citation from Corning or from ITU-T. The sheet prints 0.36 dB/km at 1310 nm, 0.01 dB/km above the 0.35 here, so hold the supplier to 0.36 in the acceptance test and read the as-built OTDR for a budget that gets signed. The row publishes NO drumM: the Corning Dimensions block prints Max. cable length per reel/drum 6000 m, a ceiling and not a putup list, and declaring it would bill a 6 km reel for a short run - measured on engine/length.js at 0.7 km of route a 6000 m drum bills 6,000 m where the 2,000 m engine default bills 2,000, and at 12 km it bills 18,000 m against 14,000; the two agree only between 4.8 and 6 km. With no drumM the engine falls back to its 2,000 m default and the purchase line carries it, so enter the reel actually ordered. What the engine does not model, and one trap. CABLE_USES has no aerial value, so aerial-ness lives in the tags and this note and nothing in the planner reads it; nothing checks span, sag, ice or wind loading, so the design will run this cable over any span you draw and the pole-to-pole distance stays a decision the planner takes; nothing metallic means nothing to bond or earth at a joint. The trap is the tie-break: cableFor answers with the SMALLEST cable that fits and breaks an equal fibre count on model id, and this model sorts before its duct twin, so a ladder naming this row beside that twin buys aerial cable for every span of that size in the plant - name this row instead of the duct twin, not beside it, unless the whole plant is on poles. This row deliberately does not say drop: isDropCable in engine/design.js reads the use field to REFUSE a span that ended up on drop cable beyond 300 m, and an aerial feeder is not tight-buffer G.657.A2 flat drop. One product data sheet, not a measured build: replace with the cable actually purchased and its as-built attenuation before ordering.
